# The Problem with LLMs 🤔 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## Think about this 🧠
### A challenge for you

:::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 28px;"}

> **You're building a chatbot for your company's HR department.**
>
> Employees will ask questions like "What's our parental leave policy?" or "How do I submit expenses?"

:::{.fragment}
**Discuss with your neighbour for 1 minute!** ⏱️

- Can ChatGPT answer these questions accurately?
- What information does it need that it doesn't have?
- How would you solve this problem?
:::

:::{.fragment}
:::{style="margin-top: 30px;"}
**The core issue**: LLMs are trained on [public internet data]{.alert}, not your company's internal documents!
:::
:::
:::

## The knowledge problem
### LLMs are frozen in time

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- LLMs are trained on data up to a [cutoff date]{.alert}
  - GPT-4: Knowledge ends around April 2023
  - Claude: Similar limitations
- They [cannot access]{.alert}:
  - Recent news and events
  - Your company's internal documents
  - Real-time data (stock prices, weather)
  - Private databases
- When asked about unknown information, LLMs often [hallucinate]{.alert}
- They present [false information with complete confidence]{.alert} 😬
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![LLM knowledge is frozen at training time](figures/frozen-knowledge.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/frozen-knowledge.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
"I was trained in 2023... what's happened since then?" 🤷
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## The hallucination problem
### Confident but wrong

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- [Hallucination]{.alert}: When an LLM generates plausible-sounding but incorrect information
- Examples:
  - Citing papers that don't exist
  - Inventing historical "facts"
  - Making up legal precedents
  - Creating fictional product features
- Why does this happen?
  - LLMs are trained to [predict likely text]{.alert}, not truth
  - They have no [ground truth]{.alert} to verify against
  - They cannot say ["I don't know"]{.alert} naturally
- This is [dangerous]{.alert} in high-stakes domains (medicine, law, finance)
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![LLM confidently hallucinating](figures/hallucination-example.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/hallucination-example.png"}

Source: [AI Incident Database](https://incidentdatabase.ai/)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## The solution: Give LLMs a library card! 📚
### Retrieval-Augmented Generation

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Instead of relying only on training data...
- [Retrieve]{.alert} relevant information from external sources
- [Augment]{.alert} the prompt with this information
- [Generate]{.alert} a response grounded in real documents
- This is called [RAG]{.alert} (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
- Benefits:
  - [Current information]{.alert}: No knowledge cutoff
  - [Accurate answers]{.alert}: Based on real documents
  - [Verifiable]{.alert}: Can cite sources
  - [Cost-effective]{.alert}: No need to retrain the model
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![RAG gives LLMs access to external knowledge](figures/rag-concept.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/rag-concept.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
Think of it as giving the LLM a "cheat sheet" for each question!
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

# Semantic Search 🔍 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## From keywords to meaning
### The evolution of search

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
**Traditional Keyword Search:**

- Matches [exact words]{.alert} in documents
- "dog food" → finds documents containing "dog" AND "food"
- Problems:
  - "canine nutrition" won't match!
  - Synonyms are missed
  - Context is ignored

:::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"}
[![Keyword search](figures/keyword-search.png){width="80%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/keyword-search.png"}
:::
:::

:::{.column width=50%}
**Semantic Search:**

- Matches based on [meaning]{.alert}
- "dog food" → finds documents about [pet nutrition]{.alert}
- Understands:
  - Synonyms ("car" ≈ "automobile")
  - Related concepts
  - Intent behind the query

:::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 20px;"}
[![Semantic search](figures/semantic-search.png){width="80%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/semantic-search.png"}
:::
:::
:::
:::

## How semantic search works
### It's all about embeddings!

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Remember [embeddings]{.alert} from our language lecture?
- Text → Vector of numbers (e.g., 768 dimensions)
- Similar meanings → [Vectors close together]{.alert}
- The process:
  1. Convert all documents to embeddings
  2. Convert the query to an embedding
  3. Find documents whose embeddings are [closest to the query]{.alert}
- This captures [semantic similarity]{.alert}, not just word overlap
- "What's the refund policy?" matches "Returns and exchanges"
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Embeddings capture semantic meaning](figures/embedding-space.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/embedding-space.png"}

Source: [Pinecone](https://www.pinecone.io/learn/)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Measuring similarity
### How close is "close"?

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- We need to measure [distance between vectors]{.alert}
- Common metrics:

**Cosine Similarity** (most popular):
$$\text{similarity} = \frac{\mathbf{A} \cdot \mathbf{B}}{||\mathbf{A}|| \times ||\mathbf{B}||}$$

- Measures the [angle]{.alert} between vectors
- Ranges from -1 (opposite) to 1 (identical)
- Ignores magnitude, focuses on direction

**Euclidean Distance**:

- Measures [straight-line distance]{.alert}
- Familiar from geometry
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Distance metrics visualised](figures/distance-metrics.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/distance-metrics.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
Cosine similarity: The angle matters, not the length!
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Vector databases
### Where embeddings live

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Traditional databases: [Find rows where column = value]{.alert}
- Vector databases: [Find vectors closest to this vector]{.alert}
- Optimised for [similarity search]{.alert} at scale
- Can search billions of vectors in milliseconds!
- Popular vector databases:
  - [Pinecone]{.alert}: Fully managed, easy to use
  - [Weaviate]{.alert}: Open source, flexible
  - [ChromaDB]{.alert}: Lightweight, great for prototyping
  - [pgvector]{.alert}: PostgreSQL extension
  - [FAISS]{.alert}: Meta's library for similarity search
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Vector database architecture](figures/vector-database.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/vector-database.png"}

Source: [Pinecone](https://www.pinecone.io/)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Approximate Nearest Neighbours (ANN)
### Speed vs accuracy trade-off

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Finding the [exact]{.alert} nearest vectors = slow (check every vector)
- [Approximate Nearest Neighbours]{.alert}: Good enough, much faster!
- Key insight: [We don't need perfection]{.alert}
  - Top 10 results ≈ correct is usually fine
- Techniques used:
  - [Indexing]{.alert}: Organise vectors for faster lookup
  - [Clustering]{.alert}: Group similar vectors together
  - [Hashing]{.alert}: Map vectors to buckets
- Result: Search billions of vectors in [milliseconds]{.alert}!
- Trade-off: Might miss the absolute best match (usually acceptable)
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![ANN vs exact search](figures/ann-search.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/ann-search.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
ANN: 99% accuracy at 1000× the speed
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

# RAG Architecture 🏗️ {background-color="#2d4563"}

## The RAG pipeline
### How it all fits together

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=100%}
```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '16px'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    A[📄 Documents] --> B[✂️ Chunking]
    B --> C[🔢 Embedding]
    C --> D[(🗄️ Vector DB)]
    
    E[❓ User Query] --> F[🔢 Embed Query]
    F --> G[🔍 Similarity Search]
    D --> G
    G --> H[📋 Retrieved Chunks]
    H --> I[📝 Augmented Prompt]
    E --> I
    I --> J[🤖 LLM]
    J --> K[💬 Response]
    
    style D fill:#90EE90,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style J fill:#87CEEB,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

:::{style="margin-top: 20px;"}
**Two phases:**

1. [Indexing]{.alert} (offline): Documents → Chunks → Embeddings → Vector database
2. [Retrieval + Generation]{.alert} (online): Query → Find similar chunks → Augment prompt → Generate answer
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Step 1: Chunking
### Breaking documents into pieces

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Documents are often [too long]{.alert} to embed directly
- We need to [split them into smaller pieces]{.alert}
- Why chunking matters:
  - [Efficiency]{.alert}: Smaller chunks = faster retrieval
  - [Relevance]{.alert}: Precise chunks = better matches
  - [Context limits]{.alert}: LLMs have maximum input lengths
- The challenge: [Balance size and meaning]{.alert}
  - Too small: Lose context
  - Too large: Dilute relevance
- Typical chunk sizes: [200-1000 tokens]{.alert}
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Document chunking](figures/chunking-overview.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/chunking-overview.png"}

Source: [Mastering LLM](https://masteringllm.medium.com/)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Chunking strategies
### There's more than one way to slice a document!

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 20px;"}

| Strategy | How it works | Best for |
|----------|--------------|----------|
| [Fixed-length]{.alert} | Split every N tokens/characters | Simple documents, FAQs |
| [Sentence-based]{.alert} | Split at sentence boundaries | Short, direct responses |
| [Paragraph-based]{.alert} | Split at paragraph breaks | Articles, reports |
| [Sliding window]{.alert} | Overlapping chunks | Context-critical documents |
| [Semantic]{.alert} | Split by meaning (using ML) | Complex technical content |
| [Recursive]{.alert} | Hierarchical (headings → paragraphs → sentences) | Structured documents |

:::{style="margin-top: 20px;"}
**Key insight**: The [best strategy depends on your documents]{.alert} and use case!
:::
:::

## Chunking visualised
### Fixed-length vs sliding window

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
**Fixed-Length Chunking:**

:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Fixed-length chunking](figures/fixed-chunking.png){width="90%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/fixed-chunking.png"}
:::

- Simple to implement
- May cut mid-sentence 😬
- Fast and predictable
:::

:::{.column width=50%}
**Sliding Window Chunking:**

:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Sliding window chunking](figures/sliding-window.png){width="90%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/sliding-window.png"}
:::

- Chunks overlap by N tokens
- Preserves context at boundaries
- Creates more chunks (storage cost)
:::
:::
:::

## Step 2: Embedding
### Converting chunks to vectors

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Each chunk is converted to a [vector embedding]{.alert}
- Popular embedding models:
  - [OpenAI text-embedding-3-large]{.alert}: 3072 dimensions
  - [Cohere Embed]{.alert}: Multilingual support
  - [BGE / E5]{.alert}: Open source alternatives
  - [Sentence-BERT]{.alert}: Classic, well-tested
- The embedding model [captures semantic meaning]{.alert}
- Same model must be used for [documents AND queries]{.alert}!
- Store embeddings in [vector database]{.alert} with metadata:
  - Source document
  - Page number
  - Section title
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Embedding process](figures/embedding-process.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/embedding-process.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
Each chunk becomes a point in high-dimensional space
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Step 3: Retrieval
### Finding the right chunks

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- User asks a question
- Question is [embedded using the same model]{.alert}
- Vector database finds the [k most similar chunks]{.alert}
- Typical k = 3 to 10 chunks
- Retrieved chunks should be:
  - [Relevant]{.alert} to the question
  - [Diverse]{.alert} (not all saying the same thing)
  - [Complete]{.alert} enough to answer
- Advanced techniques:
  - [Hybrid search]{.alert}: Combine semantic + keyword
  - [Re-ranking]{.alert}: Use a second model to refine results
  - [Query expansion]{.alert}: Generate multiple query variations
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Retrieval process](figures/retrieval-process.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/retrieval-process.png"}

Source: [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/)
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Step 4: Augmented generation
### Putting context in the prompt

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Combine [retrieved chunks + user question]{.alert} into a prompt
- Example augmented prompt:

```
Use the following context to answer the question.
If you cannot find the answer in the context,
say "I don't have that information."

Context:
[Chunk 1: Company policy states that...]
[Chunk 2: The deadline for submissions is...]
[Chunk 3: Employees are entitled to...]

Question: What is the parental leave policy?

Answer:
```

- The LLM generates a response [grounded in the context]{.alert}
- Can cite sources: "According to the HR policy document..."
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Augmented prompt structure](figures/augmented-prompt.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/augmented-prompt.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
The magic: LLM + relevant context = accurate, sourced answers!
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

# Building RAG Systems 🔧 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## Real-world RAG applications
### Where RAG shines

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}

| Domain | Application | Example |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| 🏢 **Enterprise** | Internal knowledge base | "What's our expense policy?" |
| ⚖️ **Legal** | Case law research | "Find precedents for this situation" |
| 🏥 **Healthcare** | Medical literature search | "Latest treatments for condition X" |
| 🛒 **E-commerce** | Product recommendations | "Find shoes similar to these" |
| 📞 **Customer support** | FAQ chatbots | "How do I reset my password?" |
| 📚 **Education** | Study assistants | "Explain this concept from the textbook" |
| 💰 **Finance** | Report analysis | "Summarise this earnings call" |

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; text-align: center;"}
[Any domain with lots of documents + questions = RAG opportunity!]{.alert}
:::
:::

## Discussion: Design a RAG system 💭
### Your turn to think!

:::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 26px;"}

> **Scenario**: Your university library wants a chatbot that can answer questions about the millions of research papers in their collection.

:::{.fragment}
**Take 2 minutes to discuss with your neighbour:** ⏱️

1. What documents would you index?
2. How would you chunk academic papers?
3. What metadata would be useful?
4. What could go wrong?
:::

:::{.fragment}
:::{style="margin-top: 20px;"}
**Hint**: Think about abstracts vs full text, citations, publication dates...
:::
:::
:::

## Common RAG pitfalls
### What can go wrong

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
**Retrieval Problems:**

- [Wrong chunks retrieved]{.alert}: Query doesn't match relevant content
- [Missing context]{.alert}: Important info split across chunks
- [Outdated documents]{.alert}: Stale information in the index

**Generation Problems:**

- [Ignoring context]{.alert}: LLM uses training data instead
- [Hallucinating beyond context]{.alert}: Making up details
- [Conflicting sources]{.alert}: Multiple chunks say different things

**System Problems:**

- [Latency]{.alert}: Too slow for real-time use
- [Cost]{.alert}: Too many API calls
- [Scale]{.alert}: Millions of documents overwhelm the system
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![RAG failure modes](figures/rag-pitfalls.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/rag-pitfalls.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
Good RAG requires careful attention to each component!
:::
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Best practices for RAG
### Making it work well

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
**Document Preparation:**

- ✅ Clean and preprocess documents
- ✅ Add meaningful metadata
- ✅ Test different chunking strategies
- ✅ Use overlap for context preservation

**Retrieval Optimisation:**

- ✅ Tune k (number of retrieved chunks)
- ✅ Consider hybrid search (semantic + keyword)
- ✅ Implement re-ranking for better precision
- ✅ Monitor and log retrieval quality
:::

:::{.column width=50%}
**Prompt Engineering:**

- ✅ Include clear instructions
- ✅ Tell LLM to cite sources
- ✅ Allow "I don't know" responses
- ✅ Handle edge cases gracefully

**Evaluation:**

- ✅ Test with real user queries
- ✅ Measure retrieval recall and precision
- ✅ Check for hallucinations
- ✅ Gather user feedback
:::
:::
:::

## RAG vs Fine-tuning
### When to use which?

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=50%}
**Use RAG when:**

- Information [changes frequently]{.alert}
- You need [citations and sources]{.alert}
- You have [limited training data]{.alert}
- You want [quick deployment]{.alert}
- [Privacy matters]{.alert} (data stays in your DB)

**Examples:**

- Customer support (FAQs change)
- Legal research (need citations)
- News summarisation (daily updates)
:::

:::{.column width=50%}
**Use Fine-tuning when:**

- You need a [specific style/format]{.alert}
- Knowledge is [stable]{.alert} and won't change
- You need [very fast inference]{.alert}
- You have [lots of training examples]{.alert}
- RAG retrieval [isn't precise enough]{.alert}

**Examples:**

- Code generation (specific language style)
- Medical terminology (domain adaptation)
- Brand voice (consistent tone)
:::
:::

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; text-align: center;"}
[Many production systems use BOTH: Fine-tuned model + RAG]{.alert} 🔥
:::
:::

## The future: Agentic RAG
### Beyond simple retrieval

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 24px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=55%}
- Current RAG: [Single retrieval → single response]{.alert}
- Agentic RAG: [Multiple retrievals, reasoning, tool use]{.alert}
- The agent can:
  - Decide [when]{.alert} to retrieve
  - Choose [which sources]{.alert} to query
  - [Verify]{.alert} information across sources
  - [Refine]{.alert} queries based on initial results
- Examples:
  - Multi-hop reasoning: "Who is older: the CEO of Apple or Google?"
  - Fact-checking: Verify claims against multiple sources
  - Research: Explore a topic deeply with follow-up queries
:::

:::{.column width=45%}
:::{style="text-align: center;"}
[![Agentic RAG architecture](figures/agentic-rag.png){width="100%"}](#){data-modal-type="image" data-modal-url="figures/agentic-rag.png"}

:::{style="font-size: 18px; margin-top: 10px;"}
The future: LLMs that know when and how to look things up!
:::

# Summary 📚 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## Main takeaways

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 26px;"}

- `r fa('brain')` LLMs have [frozen knowledge]{.alert} and can hallucinate—RAG solves this!

- `r fa('search')` [Semantic search]{.alert} finds documents by meaning, not just keywords, using embeddings

- `r fa('database')` [Vector databases]{.alert} store embeddings and enable fast similarity search

- `r fa('scissors')` [Chunking]{.alert} breaks documents into retrievable pieces—strategy matters!

- `r fa('cogs')` RAG pipeline: [Chunk → Embed → Store → Retrieve → Augment → Generate]{.alert}

- `r fa('check-circle')` Best practices: Clean data, good chunking, clear prompts, allow "I don't know"

- `r fa('rocket')` The future is [agentic RAG]{.alert}: LLMs that reason about when and what to retrieve
:::

## Further reading

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 22px;"}
:::{.columns}

**Required:**

- AWS (2025). [What is RAG?](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/retrieval-augmented-generation/) Comprehensive beginner's guide.
- Mastering LLM (2024). [11 Chunking Strategies for RAG](https://masteringllm.medium.com/11-chunking-strategies-for-rag-simplified-visualized-df0dbec8e373). Visual explanations of chunking.
- Slack (2025). [Semantic Search Explained](https://slack.com/blog/productivity/semantic-search-explained-how-it-works-and-why-it-matters). How semantic search works.

**Recommended:**

- Pinecone. [What is a Vector Database?](https://www.pinecone.io/learn/vector-database/) Deep dive into vector DBs.
- LangChain. [RAG Tutorial](https://python.langchain.com/docs/tutorials/rag/). Hands-on implementation guide.
